narrativeReportMd:
# StructureDefinition R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
The artifact identity is stable and there are no local element removals or cardinality tightenings, but R6 introduces local StructureDefinition validation changes and metadata changes that matter for conformance tooling. The clearest hard break is `sdf-30`: R6 rejects `contentReference` in constrained differentials, and the local R4 core package contains a concrete affected profile (`shareablecodesystem`).

## Scope
This report is scoped to the `StructureDefinition` resource definition itself. Inherited `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, and `BackboneElement` changes are excluded and listed as out of scope. Changes inside `ElementDefinition` are delegated, except where R6 adds local StructureDefinition invariants that validate `snapshot.element` or `differential.element`.

## Main migration themes
The main migration themes are: stricter authoring invariants for StructureDefinition resources; R6-to-R4 loss for new optional metadata elements; and terminology/tooling risk from the move from R4 `defined-types` to R6 `fhir-types`. Semantic migration is also needed for `jurisdiction`, whose meaning shifts toward maintainer authority rather than intended use.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is `StructureDefinition:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:StructureDefinition-root:sdf30-contentReference`, a hard validation break with a local R4 core example. `StructureDefinition:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:StructureDefinition.type:types-vs-fhir-types` is a high tooling/runtime risk because many R4 core type names are not R6 `fhir-types`. Conditional invariants `sdf-27` and `sdf-28` are potential hard breaks, but local core scans found no affected examples.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for cross-version type handling, for any legacy profiles using differential `contentReference`, and for deciding whether `jurisdiction` values in existing registries mean maintainer jurisdiction or intended deployment jurisdiction.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most changes are understandable for native R6 authoring. Less disruptive alternatives would have included warning-first transitions for some invariants, a version-aware or legacy-compatible type binding, and explicit cross-version extensions for new metadata fields.

## Follow-up analysis
Review `ElementDefinition`, `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, and the `fhir-types`/FHIR-version terminology artifacts separately. Official narrative diffs and terminology expansions would improve confidence.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `StructureDefinition` keeps the same identity and has no local removals or existing-element cardinality tightenings, but R6 adds validation invariants and metadata that create real migration risk. Top concerns are the hard `sdf-30` break for constrained differentials using `contentReference`, the move from R4 `defined-types` to R6 `fhir-types`, and semantic reinterpretation of `jurisdiction`. The largest uncertainty is prevalence in non-core IGs and how strict target tooling is about extensible bindings and warnings.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be validator-first: scan StructureDefinitions for differential `contentReference`, missing `derivation` when `baseDefinition` is present, and under-described slicing. Tooling should be version-aware for `StructureDefinition.type` rather than assuming the R6 `fhir-types` value set covers historical R4 metadata. R6-to-R4 transforms need explicit handling for `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `copyrightLabel`, and newer `fhirVersion` codes. Registry semantics for `jurisdiction` should be reviewed rather than blindly copied.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable local deltas because both primary StructureDefinition JSON files and package metadata were available and parsed. Confidence is medium for terminology and prevalence judgments because no terminology-server expansions, official narrative diffs, Jira notes, or broad non-core IG corpus were available. A local core corpus scan was used to calibrate several invariants and found one concrete `sdf-30` R4 core hit.

findings.title: StructureDefinition.type now binds to R6 fhir-types instead of the R4 defined-types union

binding.description: Either a resource or a data type, including logical model types.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `StructureDefinition.type` used an extensible binding to `defined-types`, composed from the R4 data type and resource type code systems.

binding.description: Either a resource or a data type, including logical model types.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local code-system comparison, not a terminology-server expansion, found 48 R4 core StructureDefinition `type` values absent from the R6 `fhir-types` code system and 37 R6 codes absent from the R4 union. The binding remains `extensible`, so this is primarily a conformance, validation-warning, and tooling compatibility change rather than a mandatory-code hard validation error.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `StructureDefinition.type` points at the consolidated `fhir-types` value set and code system. That list reflects R6's type/resource inventory, including new infrastructure types and excluding several R4 artifacts that were removed, renamed, or replaced.

facts.note: Computed from local R4 StructureDefinition files and R6 CodeSystem-fhir-types.json.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are unchanged; only the binding value set changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the binding is extensible, an R4 instance with an out-of-R6-list `type` is not automatically invalid solely from the binding. The practical break is in validators, registries, and code generators that treat the R6 `fhir-types` inventory as the authoritative set of known artifacts. The local R4 core corpus contains 48 StructureDefinition `type` values that are not R6 `fhir-types`, so R4-era definitions for removed or renamed resources are likely to produce warnings, rejection by strict tooling, or no generated target class in R6-oriented pipelines.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: This is business-risk relevant for conformance registries and tooling that must retain historical R4 definitions while running R6 metadata validation.

justification.inferredGoal: Align StructureDefinition.type with the R6 unified FHIR type inventory.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: A version-tolerant base binding could retain historical R4 type names while distinguishing native R6 types.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of using a unified current `fhir-types` inventory is reasonable for native R6 authoring, validation, and code generation. A less disruptive design is possible, but it is only partial because `StructureDefinition.type` must also tell R6 tooling whether the type is actually available in the R6 model. Treating historical and current type names as one base binding would reduce migration warnings but create ambiguity for generators and registries.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would bind `StructureDefinition.type` to a version-tolerant value set that includes current R6 codes plus retained historical R4 codes, ideally with status/version metadata or a companion current-release profile. That would preserve many R4 definitions, but tools would still need to branch on `fhirVersion` before generating classes or validating native R6 artifacts, so the alternative has material interoperability and implementation cost.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy metadata but materially weakens the current-release type signal and adds version-aware tooling burden.

evidence.detail: R4 binding is extensible to ValueSet/defined-types.
R6 binding is extensible to ValueSet/fhir-types.

evidence.locator: CodeSystem-fhir-types.json and R4 data-types/resource-types code systems
evidence.detail: Local code comparison found 48 R4 core StructureDefinition type values absent from R6 fhir-types, including SimpleQuantity, ClinicalImpression, DocumentManifest, and TestScript.

examples.examplesMd: An R4 StructureDefinition with `type: "ClinicalImpression"` remains structurally a `StructureDefinition`, but R6 type-aware tooling no longer sees `ClinicalImpression` as an R6 FHIR type. The binding is extensible, so this should be treated as a high tooling/conformance risk rather than a simple mandatory-code validation failure.

findings.narrativeMd: `StructureDefinition.type` is the key discriminator used by validators, package indexes, registries, and generated model code to decide what a StructureDefinition defines or constrains. R6 changes its terminology universe from the R4 data-types/resource-types union to the R6 `fhir-types` code system. That is appropriate for native R6 artifacts but risky for cross-version repositories: many valid R4 type names are no longer R6 type names, while many R6 type names cannot be understood by R4 tooling.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Base FHIR validation should not make this a hard error by itself because the binding strength is `extensible`. However, terminology validation can produce new warnings, strict implementations may promote those warnings to failures, and code generators may fail to locate model classes for R4-only type names. R6-native type names such as `CodeableReference` and `integer64` are not cleanly representable as R4 `defined-types` codes.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Cross-version tooling should preserve the original FHIR release context for each StructureDefinition and should not validate `type` against only the current R6 `fhir-types` list when processing R4 packages. Build a version-aware type map, and test R4 definitions for removed/renamed resources and datatypes explicitly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 binding could have been made less disruptive by binding to a versioned union or by publishing an authoritative mapping for historical type codes. That would preserve old metadata at the cost of a less precise current-release type inventory.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology impact was assessed by comparing local CodeSystem files, not by asking a terminology server to expand the value sets.

findings.title: New sdf-30 invariant rejects contentReference in constrained differentials

oldState.summary: No root invariant prohibited differential.element.contentReference when derivation was constraint.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed a constraint-profile differential to contain an ElementDefinition with `contentReference`. The local R4 core package contains `StructureDefinition-shareablecodesystem.json` with `derivation: constraint` and a differential element `CodeSystem.concept.concept` using `contentReference: #CodeSystem.concept`.

newState.summary: R6 adds error invariant sdf-30: differential contentReference requires derivation = specialization.

constraints.human: ContentReferences can only be defined in specializations, not constrained types

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes this pattern invalid for constraint profiles. A profile differential can no longer introduce or restate `contentReference`; that construct must appear only in specializations.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break. An R4 StructureDefinition resource that was valid enough to be packaged in the R4 core distribution can fail R6 validation because the new root invariant evaluates the differential and rejects `contentReference` unless the StructureDefinition is a specialization.

justification.inferredGoal: Keep constraint-profile differentials from redefining recursive content model structure.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Allow only legacy constraint differentials whose `contentReference` exactly restates the base recursive structure, or warn first.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of preventing constrained profiles from redefining recursive content models is reasonable, and a hard invariant is understandable for clean R6 authoring. The known R4 core hit shows real breakage, so this is not fully cost-free. However, the main less-breaking alternative depends on resolving and comparing base definitions, which is more complex than a self-contained invariant and may not cover profiles that used `contentReference` to change structure.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base-design alternative would permit `contentReference` in a constraint differential only when it is demonstrably equivalent to the inherited base relationship, while rejecting changed or newly introduced recursive references. A warning-only transition would be even less disruptive but would not enforce the R6 rule. These alternatives reduce migration failures for redundant R4 patterns, but they add validator complexity and ambiguity.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve safe legacy cases but requires base-aware comparison and could keep a confusing deprecated authoring pattern alive.

evidence.detail: R6 adds an error invariant prohibiting differential contentReference unless derivation is specialization.
The R4 core package has a constraint StructureDefinition with contentReference '#CodeSystem.concept' in its differential.

examples.examplesMd: The example is reduced from the local R4 core `shareablecodesystem` profile to show the relevant `derivation` plus `contentReference` combination.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a hard invariant that changes how recursive content definitions may appear in StructureDefinition differentials. The concrete local impact is not hypothetical: the R4 core package contains a shareable CodeSystem profile that uses `contentReference` in a constrained differential. Such a StructureDefinition can no longer be accepted unchanged by an R6 validator.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is old-valid/new-invalid for at least one local R4 core artifact. The failure is at StructureDefinition validation time, before any resource instance conforming to the profile is evaluated. R6-to-R4 representability is not the main issue; the main issue is loading or migrating R4 profiles into R6 tooling.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Migration should scan differentials for `contentReference` when `derivation` is `constraint`. Where the content reference merely repeats base structure, remove it from the differential and rely on snapshot generation from the base. If the profile intended to alter recursive structure, manual redesign is needed because R6 disallows that in constrained types.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A warning or conditional allowance for base-equivalent content references would have been less disruptive. The hard error is probably justified for native R6 authoring clarity, but it is avoidable for legacy-profile ingestion.

findings.title: New sdf-27 invariant requires derivation whenever baseDefinition is present

oldState.summary: StructureDefinition.derivation remained 0..1 and no invariant directly required it when baseDefinition existed.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `baseDefinition` and `derivation` were both optional elements. Non-abstract StructureDefinitions needed a `baseDefinition` via `sdf-4`, but there was no separate error saying that a present `baseDefinition` must be accompanied by `derivation`.

newState.summary: R6 adds error invariant sdf-27: baseDefinition.exists() implies derivation.exists().

constraints.human: If there's a base definition, there must be a derivation

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the element cardinality as `0..1`, but strengthens the root validation rule so `derivation` becomes conditionally mandatory whenever `baseDefinition` is populated.

facts.note: No local R4 core StructureDefinition had baseDefinition without derivation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This can be a hard validation error for R4 StructureDefinition instances that populated `baseDefinition` but omitted `derivation`. The local R4 core package had no such examples, so prevalence in well-formed packages appears low, but custom authoring tools that treated `derivation` as inferable can be affected.

justification.inferredGoal: Make the relationship to the base explicit and avoid ambiguous profile/specialization interpretation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Warn or infer `derivation` only in narrow, unambiguous legacy cases.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Requiring `derivation` when `baseDefinition` is present addresses a real ambiguity in the StructureDefinition relationship. The local R4 core package had no affected examples, and R4 already exposed the field, so the compatibility cost appears limited. A less-breaking approach exists, but it cannot reliably preserve every omitted-derivation case without guessing author intent.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial alternative would keep the base cardinality optional and issue a warning, or infer `constraint`/`specialization` only when type, base, and kind make the answer unambiguous. That would help legacy metadata stores, but ambiguous artifacts would still need manual correction and different tools could infer different meanings.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces rare migration failures but risks inconsistent interpretation of whether a definition is a constraint or specialization.

evidence.detail: R4 `derivation` cardinality is 0..1 and no sdf-27 invariant exists.
R6 adds an error requiring derivation when baseDefinition exists.
A local scan of 658 R4 StructureDefinition files found 0 instances with baseDefinition present and derivation absent.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is illustrative only; a complete StructureDefinition would need valid snapshot or differential content. The relevant change is the omission of `derivation` while `baseDefinition` is present.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 turns an implied authoring expectation into a hard invariant. This is unlikely to affect well-formed core R4 artifacts, but it can break repositories that stored partially specified or tool-inferred StructureDefinitions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 StructureDefinition with `baseDefinition` and no `derivation` can become invalid in R6. This does not create a major R6-to-R4 representability issue because R4 can carry `derivation` if present.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Before validating R4 StructureDefinitions with R6 rules, scan for `baseDefinition` without `derivation`. Populate `derivation` explicitly based on author intent; do not infer blindly for ambiguous artifacts.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The invariant is probably justified, but a warning-first transition or well-defined inference rule would have been less disruptive for legacy metadata stores.

findings.title: Snapshot slicing now requires either a discriminator or a description

oldState.summary: No local StructureDefinition invariant required slicing.discriminator or slicing.description on snapshot elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not have this StructureDefinition-level error constraint on `snapshot.element`.

newState.summary: R6 adds error invariant sdf-28 on snapshot.element.

constraints.human: If there are no discriminators, there must be a definition

newState.narrativeMd: Any snapshot element with a `slicing` component must now include either at least one discriminator or a slicing description.

facts.note: No local R4 core snapshot slicing entries lacked both discriminator and description.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a hard validation error when it fires, but the local R4 core package had no examples. The affected pattern is likely custom/generated profiles with a syntactically present `slicing` object but no computable discriminator and no human description.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure slicing can be understood by validators or at least documented for humans.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use warning-level validation for legacy snapshots with slicing but no discriminator or description.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable because slicing without either a computable discriminator or a human description is hard for validators and implementers to understand. The less-breaking option is mainly to warn rather than reject. That preserves R4 artifacts but does not meet the stronger R6 goal of ensuring interpretable slicing in accepted snapshots.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A warning-only invariant would be the best compatibility-preserving base design. It would identify the authoring defect while allowing old snapshots to load. The tradeoff is material: downstream tools could continue consuming slicing declarations that are not computable and not documented, which undermines the conformance-quality goal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves incomplete legacy snapshots but lets ambiguous slicing continue to circulate.

evidence.detail: R6 adds the slicing discriminator/description invariant.
A local scan found 0 R4 core snapshot elements with slicing present and both discriminator and description absent.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is illustrative; the key issue is `slicing` without either `discriminator` or `description`.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes incomplete slicing metadata invalid at the StructureDefinition level. This improves authoring quality but can reject older generated snapshots that carried an empty or minimally populated `slicing` object.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid custom StructureDefinitions with under-specified slicing can become R6-invalid. R6 content that satisfies the new rule remains representable in R4 because R4 already has fields for discriminator and description.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan snapshots for `slicing` objects. Add a discriminator when slicing is computable; otherwise add a clear `slicing.description` explaining the slicing rule before R6 validation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The stricter rule is probably justified for authoring quality. A warning-only rule would have been less disruptive but would not guarantee interpretable slicing.

findings.title: R6 adds optional choice element StructureDefinition.versionAlgorithm[x]

oldState.summary: No versionAlgorithm element existed in R4.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 StructureDefinition had `version` but no computable or coded mechanism for comparing version strings.

newState.summary: Optional 0..1 choice element versionAlgorithm[x] with string and Coding choices.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can state how version strings should be ordered, either as a FHIRPath expression string or as a coded algorithm.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The element is optional, so R4 instances remain valid with respect to this addition when moving forward. The risk is reverse direction and code generation: R6 instances may carry a new choice element that R4 serializers, JSON schemas, generated classes, and summary projections do not know how to store.

justification.inferredGoal: Support deterministic comparison of artifact versions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: this optional R6 addition does not invalidate R4 StructureDefinition instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional `versionAlgorithm[x]` is a normal forward-compatible base-model change that supports deterministic version ordering without requiring existing R4 instances to change. The compatibility concern is R6-to-R4 loss, not avoidable R4-to-R6 breakage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base-design alternative needs to be counted here. Carrying the value in an R4 extension can mitigate down-conversion, but that is ordinary migration tooling rather than evidence that the R6 base model should have avoided the optional element.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extension backports are conversion mitigations, not less-breaking base R6 designs.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `versionAlgorithm[x]` as 0..1 with string and Coding choices.

examples.examplesMd: An R4 parser without extensions has no native `versionAlgorithmString` or `versionAlgorithmCoding` element.

findings.narrativeMd: `versionAlgorithm[x]` is a useful R6 addition but introduces a new choice element into an infrastructure resource used heavily by code generators and registries. The forward R4-to-R6 path is safe because the element is optional; the reverse path is lossy unless an extension or sidecar mapping is used.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid StructureDefinitions do not become invalid because of this optional addition. R6 StructureDefinitions that use it are not natively representable in R4 and may be rejected by strict R4 JSON parsers or generated R4 classes.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R6-to-R4 transforms should map `versionAlgorithm[x]` to an extension or omit it with an explicit loss note. Test both `versionAlgorithmString` and `versionAlgorithmCoding` JSON choice names.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change follows the least disruptive FHIR pattern for forward compatibility. A standardized cross-version extension would improve reverse compatibility.

findings.title: R6 adds optional StructureDefinition.copyrightLabel

oldState.summary: No copyrightLabel element existed in R4.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 only had the broader `copyright` markdown/string element for rights text.

newState.summary: Optional 0..1 string for a short copyright holder/year label.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds a short rendering label intended for page footers and generated representations.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This optional addition does not break R4-to-R6 validation. Reverse conversion can lose a short rendering label because R4 has no native field for it, though the information can usually be merged into `copyright` or represented by extension.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate compact copyright display text from full rights narrative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: this optional R6 field is forward-compatible for R4-to-R6 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of separating a compact rendering label from full rights text is reasonable, and the field is optional. It does not make R4 StructureDefinitions invalid in R6; the remaining risk is only loss or parser rejection when projecting R6 content back to R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: An extension can preserve `copyrightLabel` during R6-to-R4 conversion, but that does not count as a backward-compatible base R6 alternative. The base R6 design uses the least disruptive shape for forward compatibility: an optional non-modifier element.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extension or `copyright` folding is a reverse-conversion mitigation, not a less-breaking R6 base design.

examples.examplesMd: Plain R4 has no native `copyrightLabel` property.

findings.narrativeMd: `copyrightLabel` is a small optional addition. It matters mainly for lossless R6-to-R4 conversion and generated UI/rendering code, not for acceptance of R4 instances by R6 validators.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain acceptable without this element. R6 instances using it are not natively representable in R4 and will be unknown to strict R4 parsers.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Backporting should either map the label to an extension or concatenate it into `copyright` with a clear transform policy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: An extension-only design would have been more backward-compatible, but a native optional element is reasonable for common rendering metadata.

findings.title: StructureDefinition.fhirVersion required binding now includes R5/R6 version codes not valid in R4

oldState.summary: Required binding to FHIR-version|4.0.1, whose CodeSystem ended at 4.0.1.

newState.summary: Required binding to FHIR-version|6.0.0-ballot4, adding R4B, R5, and R6 version codes.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local CodeSystem comparison shows all R4 4.0.1 codes retained and many later version codes added.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can explicitly identify StructureDefinitions targeting R4B, R5, and R6 ballot/final versions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4-to-R6 is safe for `fhirVersion` because R4's `4.0.1` code remains present in the R6 CodeSystem. Reverse conversion is not lossless: a native R6 StructureDefinition with `fhirVersion: 6.0.0-ballot4` violates the R4 required binding.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow R6 StructureDefinitions to declare their target FHIR release.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the required value set is widened for newer releases while retaining R4 codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A FHIR release code system must evolve as new releases appear. Because the R6 binding retains R4 version codes, this is not a less-breaking R4-to-R6 base-design problem; it is an expected one-way terminology evolution that affects R6-to-R4 representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: There is no relevant less-breaking base R6 alternative to count. Omitting new R6 version codes would fail the goal of declaring R6-targeting StructureDefinitions, while mapping them to R4 extensions or sidecars is a down-conversion strategy rather than a base design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Older R4 value sets cannot natively contain future release codes; extensions only mitigate down-conversion.

evidence.detail: The R6 code system includes `6.0.0-ballot4`; the R4 code system does not.

examples.examplesMd: The assigned R6 StructureDefinition itself uses the R6 package/version context; that target version code cannot satisfy the R4 required binding.

findings.narrativeMd: `fhirVersion` is a required-binding code, so new release codes create a one-way compatibility boundary. R4 metadata can move forward because its code is retained, but R6 metadata cannot be represented as an R4-native code without loss or extension.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid `fhirVersion=4.0.1` instance becomes invalid in R6 because that code remains allowed. R6 instances using later codes are R6-valid but R4-invalid under required terminology validation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R6-to-R4 transforms should either omit `fhirVersion`, map it to an extension preserving the exact R6 code, or keep the artifact in an R6-aware package rather than pretending it is R4-native.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This is an unavoidable consequence of adding new FHIR releases. A ConceptMap or cross-version extension can document conversion but cannot make the R6 code part of the old R4 required value set.

findings.title: StructureDefinition.jurisdiction shifts from intended-use jurisdiction to maintaining-authority jurisdiction

oldState.summary: Jurisdiction was defined as the legal/geographic region where the StructureDefinition is intended to be used.

semanticText.short: Intended jurisdiction for structure definition (if applicable)
semanticText.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the structure definition is intended to be used.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 framed `jurisdiction` as an intended-use region.

newState.summary: Jurisdiction is defined as the legal/geographic region of the maintaining authority, with useContext recommended for intended jurisdictions.

semanticText.short: Jurisdiction of the authority that maintains the structure definition (if applicable)
semanticText.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating.
semanticText.comment: DEPRECATION NOTE: For consistency, implementations are encouraged to migrate to using the new 'jurisdiction' code in the useContext element.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 treats `jurisdiction` as maintainer jurisdiction and points intended/use jurisdictions toward `useContext`.

facts.oldValue: Intended jurisdiction for structure definition (if applicable)
facts.newValue: Jurisdiction of the authority that maintains the structure definition (if applicable)

impact.impactRationaleMd: The structure and binding strength are unchanged enough that this is not a hard validation break. The risk is semantic: systems that used R4 `jurisdiction` to mean where a profile applies may misclassify R6 artifacts, because R6 says the element identifies the maintaining authority's jurisdiction and recommends `useContext` for additional/intended jurisdictions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Jurisdictional applicability can drive implementation guide selection, regulatory reporting, and deployment eligibility.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify governance jurisdiction and move usage context to the general useContext mechanism.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `jurisdiction` as intended-use jurisdiction and add a distinct maintainer/authority jurisdiction element or profile guidance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying maintainer authority is a reasonable R6 goal, but reusing the existing `jurisdiction` element for a different primary meaning creates a semantic break for R4 registries that stored intended-use jurisdictions. A less-breaking base design could preserve the R4 meaning and add a new maintainer-specific element, so the same goal appears achievable with moderate rather than prohibitive tradeoff.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative is to leave `StructureDefinition.jurisdiction` with its R4 intended-use meaning and add an optional `maintainerJurisdiction` or similarly named field for the authority's operating jurisdiction, with `useContext` guidance for additional usage contexts. This introduces another jurisdiction-like representation and may require UI/search rules to distinguish the fields, but it preserves existing R4 semantics instead of silently changing what old data means.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds model surface and possible overlap with `useContext`, but avoids silent reinterpretation of existing jurisdiction data.

evidence.detail: R4 definition: legal/geographic region in which the structure definition is intended to be used.
R6 definition points to the authority that maintains the resource and recommends migrating intended jurisdiction to useContext.

examples.examplesMd: If `US` meant intended deployment jurisdiction in R4, the R6 migration may need to preserve it as a jurisdictional `useContext`, not only as `StructureDefinition.jurisdiction`.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a semantic break rather than a shape break. The same repeated CodeableConcept element remains, but the R6 definition changes what the data is supposed to mean. Existing R4 registries that filter StructureDefinitions by intended jurisdiction need to revisit those rules.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Instances generally remain structurally valid in both versions. The compatibility issue is behavioral: search, filtering, governance, and implementation-guide selection logic can produce different results if it assumes the R4 meaning in an R6 context.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review every use of `StructureDefinition.jurisdiction`. If it means intended use, populate the R6 `useContext` jurisdiction coding as well. If it means publisher/maintainer authority, keep it in `jurisdiction`. Do not blindly copy filters from R4 registries into R6 registries.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A new element for maintainer jurisdiction would have been more backward-compatible but less economical. Reusing `useContext` is a reasonable design, but it needs explicit migration guidance.

findings.title: R6 adds a canonical URL warning for pipe, hash, and space characters

oldState.summary: No local warning constraint on `url` for `|`, `#`, or spaces.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 described canonical URL stability but did not include this computable warning on the element.

newState.summary: R6 adds warning cnl-1: URL should not contain |, #, or space.

constraints.human: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

newState.narrativeMd: R6 validators can now warn when canonical URLs contain characters that interfere with canonical-reference version and fragment syntax.

facts.note: No local R4 core StructureDefinition.url contained |, #, or space.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The constraint is warning-level, so it is not a hard instance break. It can still affect CI pipelines or registries that treat warnings as failures, and it flags a real runtime issue because `|` and `#` have special meaning in canonical references.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R6 uses a warning-level canonical URL rule rather than making old instances invalid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The rule addresses a real parsing ambiguity for canonical references, and R6 calibrated it as a warning. Under base validation this is not an old-valid/new-invalid break, so a less-breaking base alternative is not materially needed.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping the guidance only in narrative text would avoid warnings in strict publication pipelines, but it would also make the rule less visible to tooling. Because the base constraint is already warning-level, this is best treated as a justified compatibility-preserving design rather than a case with a meaningful backward-compatible alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Narrative-only guidance would be quieter but would not provide computable canonical hygiene.

evidence.detail: R6 adds warning cnl-1 on StructureDefinition.url.

examples.examplesMd: The example would trigger a warning rather than a base validation error; it is included to illustrate the parsing issue.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes a previously narrative canonical hygiene rule computable. This is a low-severity change, but canonical URLs are infrastructure identifiers; warnings here can matter in package publication and registry workflows.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not old-valid/new-invalid under normal FHIR validation because severity is `warning`. It may be runtime-breaking only for pipelines configured to reject warnings.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan canonical URLs for `|`, `#`, and spaces. Mint clean replacement canonicals where possible; if an old URL is already published, keep redirects or alias mappings so references continue to resolve.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The warning-level approach is backward-compatible enough. Making this a hard error would have been more disruptive.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, abstract flag, baseDefinition, and derivation remain stable. The R6 path exists at the expected filename, so no rename/split/merge identity issue was found.
No existing local StructureDefinition element changed min/max cardinality. The only element-presence changes are the two optional additions reported as findings.

Existing local element type arrays did not remove or replace types. The only new type surface is the added `versionAlgorithm[x]` choice, and `StructureDefinition.type` terminology changed as reported separately.
No local StructureDefinition element has a changed Reference target profile. The resource primarily references canonical/uri/code/datatype fields rather than FHIR Reference targets.
No local fixed, pattern, or defaultValue constraints were added, removed, or changed.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, regex, or comparable value-limit change was found on existing elements.
No existing local modifier flag changed. `StructureDefinition.status` remains a modifier in both R4 and R6. Inherited modifier flag changes are out of scope.
No existing local summary flag changed materially. The added `versionAlgorithm[x]` is a summary element and is covered by its finding.
No slicing structure exists directly in the StructureDefinition resource aside from constraints that govern `snapshot.element.slicing`; the new `sdf-28` invariant is reported as a finding.
JSON/XML serialization was assessed from StructureDefinition element definitions, not by running generated schemas. New native elements are reported as R6-to-R4 serialization risks.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Name warning moved from sdf-0 to cnl-0 and now requires at least two characters
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The rule is warning-level in both releases. A local scan found no R4 core StructureDefinitions with a single-character `name`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code-generation pipelines that fail on warnings should check names against the R6 expression `^[A-Z]([A-Za-z0-9_]){1,254}$`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Extension context invariant is relaxed for type Extension with a non-Extension baseDefinition
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R6 expression adds `baseDefinition != 'http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Extension'` as a pass condition, so it does not invalidate R4 instances. Local package scans found no examples relying on the relaxation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 StructureDefinitions that rely on this relaxation may not validate under R4 rules without adding explicit context.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Root element label/code prohibition is relaxed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 prohibited root `label`, `code`, and `requirements`; R6 only prohibits root `requirements`. This is a relaxation for R4-to-R6 migration.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 snapshots/differentials that use root `label` or `code` may not be R4-representable. Local R6 core StructureDefinitions did not show this pattern.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds CodeableReference placement invariants sdf-24 and sdf-25
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `CodeableReference` is not an R4 datatype, and local R4 core StructureDefinitions had no CodeableReference snapshot patterns. These are native R6 authoring rules rather than R4-to-R6 migration breaks.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: When authoring R6 snapshots, put target profiles and concept bindings on the `CodeableReference` element itself, not on `.reference` or `.concept` children.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds warning-level best-practice invariants for profile root mustSupport and resource cardinality shapes
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both `sdf-26` and `sdf-29` are warnings, not errors. They can affect publication QA but not ordinary conformance validity unless a pipeline escalates warnings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Profile publishers should avoid root `mustSupport=true` and ensure resource/complex-type specializations use `0`/`1` minimums and `1`/`*` maximums in differential elements.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: FHIR-defined type-code invariant is normalized and slightly tightened
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 uses one expression over `(differential | snapshot)` and removes the R4 snapshot allowance for dotted FHIR type codes, while keeping the FHIRPath System exception. A local scan found zero R4 or R6 core hits for non-FHIRPath dotted type codes.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Custom HL7-canonical StructureDefinitions with dotted snapshot type codes should be checked manually even though no local core examples were found.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 snapshots explicitly carry mustSupport=false on many elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Absence of `mustSupport` in R4 and explicit `false` in R6 have the same effective meaning for base definitions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Diff tools should normalize missing boolean flags to false to avoid reporting noise.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `StructureDefinition.snapshot.element` and `differential.element` are typed as `ElementDefinition`; nested ElementDefinition field additions/removals are not owned by this report except for local StructureDefinition invariants.
Inherited changes such as `Resource.language` binding strength are out of scope here but affect all resources including StructureDefinition.
Inherited DomainResource elements and modifierExtension/text/contained semantics should be assessed in the DomainResource report.
The `StructureDefinition.type` finding depends on the R6 `fhir-types` terminology and would benefit from an authoritative expansion and cross-version ConceptMap.
R6-to-R4 representability of `fhirVersion` depends on version-code terminology evolution.
